join_order.notes: title.id is dense identity, so candidate mv → title row index = mv-1. Apply production_year > 2005 inline.
For each surviving movie, use movie_info__movie_id offsets to fetch mi rows; existence test against IN-set; early break on first hit.

data_structures.candidate_movies: absl/flat_hash_set<int32_t> (or std::unordered_set) pre-sized ~16384; alternatively bitset over title.id range if memory allows (2.5M bits = 316KB)

parallelism.rationale: Total work is tiny (~10K candidate movies, ~63K mi varlen probes, 30 keyword CSR walks). Thread setup and synchronization overhead would exceed compute cost.

indexes.purpose: join_lookup: candidate movie → mi row range for IN existence test

execution_notes: Step 1: scan keyword/keyword.{off,dat} once; for each row with len>=6 run memmem for 'sequel'; collect id = row_index + 1 into seq_ids.

Step 2: for each kid in seq_ids, range [off[kid], off[kid+1]) in movie_keyword__keyword_id__rowids gives mk_row positions; read movie_keyword/movie_id.bin[mk_row] and insert into candidate_movies set.
Step 3: iterate candidate_movies; for each mv compute idx = mv-1; check title/production_year.bin[idx]: skip if INT32_MIN or <=2005; push survivors into vector.
Step 4: sort survivors ascending (so movie_info access is sequential — movie_info is FK-sorted by movie_id, improving HDD readahead and cache locality).

Step 5: for each mv in survivors, range [mi_off[mv], mi_off[mv+1]) in movie_info/info.{off,dat}; per row, len = info.off[r+1]-info.off[r]; if len not in {6,7,9} skip; else compare via flat_hash_set<string_view>. On first match, fetch t.title at idx mv-1 and update MIN; break inner loop.
Step 6: emit final MIN string (empty result handling: print NULL if no matches).
